title: Others reject mode two and allow modes one and three—image loved per se as a means for the end
source_text: VIII. Contra vero nonnulli sunt qui rejiciunt secundum illum adorandi modum, in quo uno & eodem adorationis actu, exemplar & imago simul, tanquam unum objectum totale adorantur; sed putant imagines posse & debere coli, non tantum primo, verum tertio quoque modo: ita ut adoratio dirigatur ad solam imaginem, tanquam rem per se adoratam; exemplar autem non nisi indirecte respiciat, nempe, ut illud propter quod imago adoratur: quanquam enim imago in se & per se adorari debeat, non tamen illam adorari, nisi propter exemplar: quemadmodum medium per se, & in se amatur, quanquam non nisi propter finem ametur.
pass_a_gloss: But on the contrary there are some who reject that second mode of adoring, in which by one and the same act of adoration exemplar and image together are adored as one total object; yet they think that images can and ought to be cultivated not only in the first, but also in the third mode: so that adoration is directed to the image alone, as a thing adored per se; but the exemplar is regarded only indirectly, namely, as that on account of which the image is adored: for although the image ought to be adored in itself and per se, yet it is not adored except on account of the exemplar: just as a means is loved per se, and in itself, although it is not loved except on account of the end.
pass_b_english: Opposite party: drop mode two’s single total object; keep modes one and three.
Image may be the per-se terminus, yet only because of the exemplar—like loving a means for an end.
